questions.prompt: A real-estate photographer is paid to shoot aerial photos of a house with a 3-pound drone. Which set of rules governs this flight?

options.text: 14 CFR part 107, because the flight is not strictly recreational
State and local rules, because the flight is over private land
The recreational exception, because it weighs under 55 pounds

questions.explanation: Paid work cannot use the recreational exception in 49 U.S.C. 44809, so the operation falls under part 107 and needs a remote pilot certificate.

questions.prompt: Within how many days must a remote pilot in command report to the FAA an operation that caused a serious injury?

options.text: 10 working days after the operation
24 hours after the operation
10 calendar days after the operation

questions.explanation: A safety event that meets the part 107.9 criteria must be reported no later than 10 calendar days after the operation.

questions.prompt: A remote pilot flies a 0.4-pound drone for paid mapping work under part 107. Does the aircraft have to be registered?

options.text: No, because a remote pilot certificate takes the place of registration
No, because aircraft weighing 0.55 pounds or less are exempt from registration
Yes, because part 107 operations require registration regardless of weight

questions.explanation: The 0.55-pound registration exception applies only to aircraft flown exclusively under the recreational statute. Part 107 operations require an effective registration.

questions.prompt: A remote pilot wants to fly in Class C airspace. What does part 107 require?

options.text: Prior authorization from the ATC facility having jurisdiction over that airspace
Two-way radio contact with the tower on its frequency throughout the flight
Notification to the tower by phone before launch and again after landing

questions.explanation: Operation in Class B, C or D, or in the surface area of Class E designated for an airport, requires prior ATC authorization.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum altitude for a small unmanned aircraft, with no waiver, when not near a structure?

options.text: 400 feet above ground level
400 feet above mean sea level
500 feet above the surface

questions.explanation: The aircraft may not fly higher than 400 feet AGL unless operated within 400 feet of a structure as described in 107.51(b).

questions.prompt: To keep exercising remote PIC privileges, how often must a remote pilot complete recurrent training or pass the initial test again?

options.text: Within the previous 12 calendar months
Within the previous 24 calendar months
Within the previous 36 calendar months

questions.explanation: A person may not exercise the privileges of a remote PIC unless they passed the initial test or completed recurrent training within the previous 24 calendar months.

questions.prompt: Which aircraft qualifies for a Category 1 operation over people?

options.text: One of 0.55 pounds or less on takeoff and in flight, with a Category 1 label and a declaration of compliance on file
One of 0.55 pounds or less on takeoff and in flight, with no exposed rotating parts that would lacerate skin
One of 0.55 pounds or less not counting payload, with no exposed rotating parts that would lacerate skin

questions.explanation: Category 1 requires 0.55 pounds or less including everything attached, and no exposed rotating parts that would lacerate skin. No label or DOC is required.

questions.prompt: What is the remote pilot's duty if a standard Remote ID aircraft stops broadcasting during a flight?

options.text: Finish if the aircraft stays in sight
Land within the next 30 minutes
Land as soon as practicable

questions.explanation: If the aircraft is no longer broadcasting the required message elements, the person manipulating the controls must land as soon as practicable.

questions.prompt: Which description fits Class B airspace?

options.text: Surrounds airports with radar approach control, with a 5 NM surface core and a 10 NM shelf
Surrounds the busiest airports, with tailored layers like an upside-down wedding cake, and needs ATC authorization
Surrounds towered airports as a single cylinder from the surface to 2,500 feet above the airport

questions.explanation: Class B surrounds the nation's busiest airports. Its configuration is tailored, usually with several layers, and a remote pilot must receive ATC authorization before flying in it.

questions.prompt: A towered airport with radar approach control has airspace with a 5 NM surface area and a 10 NM outer ring starting at 1,200 feet above the airport. What class is it?

options.text: Class C
Class D
Class G

questions.explanation: Class C typically has a 5 NM radius surface area and a 10 NM outer circle from 1,200 feet to 4,000 feet above the airport elevation. Authorization is required to fly a small UA there.

questions.prompt: Class D airspace generally extends from the surface to what height above the airport elevation?

options.text: 2,500 feet
4,000 feet
700 feet

questions.explanation: Class D generally extends from the surface to 2,500 feet above the airport elevation and surrounds airports with an operating control tower.

questions.prompt: A dashed magenta line on a sectional chart around an airport marks what?

options.text: Class D airspace that extends from the surface
Class E airspace that begins at the surface
Class E airspace that begins at 700 feet AGL

questions.explanation: Dashed magenta shows Class E airspace with a floor at the surface (a surface area designated for an airport). A small UA needs ATC authorization inside it.

questions.prompt: Class G airspace is best described as:

options.text: Controlled airspace from 18,000 feet MSL up to and including FL 600
Controlled airspace from the surface up to the floor of overlying Class A
Uncontrolled airspace from the surface up to the overlying Class E base

questions.explanation: Class G is the portion of airspace not designated as A, B, C, D or E. It extends from the surface to the base of the overlying Class E.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes a restricted area?

options.text: Airspace that may have a high volume of pilot training or unusual aerial activity
Airspace extending from 3 NM off the coast, where nonparticipating pilots are warned of danger
Airspace with often invisible hazards, such as artillery firing, where flight is not wholly prohibited

questions.explanation: Restricted areas contain unusual hazards like artillery or missiles. Entry requires permission from the using or controlling agency.

questions.prompt: How is a temporary flight restriction (TFR) communicated to pilots?

options.text: By a new chart line
By a NOTAM
By a METAR remark

questions.explanation: A TFR is designated by a NOTAM that starts with the words FLIGHT RESTRICTIONS and gives the location, times, area and altitudes affected.

questions.prompt: Which combination matches the basic weather minimums for a part 107 flight?

options.text: 3 statute miles visibility, 500 feet below clouds, 2,000 feet horizontally from clouds
5 statute miles visibility, 1,000 feet below clouds, 1 statute mile horizontally from clouds
1 statute mile visibility, 500 feet below clouds, 2,000 feet horizontally from clouds

questions.explanation: The part 107 weather minimums are 3 SM flight visibility from the control station, 500 feet below and 2,000 feet horizontally from clouds.

questions.prompt: Where can a remote pilot get an official weather and NOTAM briefing over the internet?

options.text: From Flight Service, for example 1800wxbrief.com
From the Aviation Weather Center, at aviationweather.gov
From the FAA TFR website, for example tfr.faa.gov

questions.explanation: Flight Service (1800wxbrief.com) provides briefings and NOTAMs. The Aviation Weather Center (aviationweather.gov) is a separate free source of reports and forecasts, not a briefing. Manufacturer apps are not a substitute.

questions.prompt: Decode this METAR: KDEN 151753Z 27015G25KT 10SM FEW080 SCT120 22/04 A3002. What is the wind?

options.text: From 270 degrees true at 15 knots, gusting to 25 knots
From 150 degrees at 27 knots, gusting to 25 knots
From 270 degrees magnetic at 15 knots with a steady speed

questions.explanation: The five-digit group gives direction in true degrees (270) and speed (15 knots); G25 means gusts to 25 knots.

questions.prompt: TAF KABC 121720Z 1218/1324 20012KT P6SM SCT040 FM122000 25015G25KT P6SM BKN030. What does 1218/1324 mean?

options.text: The forecast is valid from 12:18 UTC to 13:24 UTC on the day it was issued
The forecast is valid from 1800 UTC on the 12th to 2400 UTC on the 13th
The forecast was issued at 1800 UTC on the 12th and runs for 24 hours

questions.explanation: The valid period gives start day/hour then end day/hour in UTC. 1218/1324 means 12th at 18Z to 13th at 24Z.

questions.prompt: What conditions result in a high density altitude?

options.text: Low elevations, high pressure, low temperatures, low humidity
High elevations, low atmospheric pressure, high temperatures, high humidity
High elevations, high atmospheric pressure, low temperatures, low humidity

questions.explanation: High density altitude means thin air. High elevation, low pressure, high temperature and high humidity all reduce air density.

questions.prompt: What is a microburst?

options.text: A rotating column of air that reaches from a thunderstorm cloud to the ground
An intense, small-scale downdraft that spreads outward at the surface
A strong, narrow updraft that feeds warm air into a rapidly building cumulus

questions.explanation: A microburst is the most severe low-level wind shear: horizontal diameter of 1 to 2 miles, lasting roughly 5 to 15 minutes, with downdrafts up to 6,000 fpm.

questions.prompt: A remote PIC adds a heavier camera to a multirotor. What is the most likely effect?

options.text: Shorter flight time, reduced climb performance and less maneuverability
No change to flight time, climb or maneuverability while below 55 pounds
Longer flight time and better climb, since the aircraft is more stable

questions.explanation: Added weight reduces performance in almost every respect: higher power demand, shorter endurance, reduced rate of climb, reduced maneuverability. The 55-pound limit is a legal limit, not a performance guarantee.

questions.prompt: What is the load factor in a level coordinated turn at 60 degrees of bank?

options.text: 2 Gs
1.4 Gs
6 Gs

questions.explanation: At 60 degrees of bank the load factor is 2 Gs, so the wing must produce twice the weight in lift to hold altitude.

questions.prompt: What does the center of gravity (CG) of an aircraft depend on?

options.text: How the weight is distributed; it moves as items are shifted, added or used up
The total weight alone; it stays put when items are shifted or added
The airframe design alone; it stays fixed at a point the manufacturer marks or lists

questions.explanation: The CG is not a fixed point marked on the aircraft. Its location depends on the distribution of weight and changes as variable load items shift or are expended.

questions.prompt: Who is responsible for determining the performance of the small unmanned aircraft for a flight?

options.text: The aircraft manufacturer
The aircraft's owner or operator
The remote pilot in command

questions.explanation: The remote PIC is responsible for the safe operation and for ensuring the aircraft is suitable for the flight conditions, using manufacturer data where available.

questions.prompt: A remote pilot plans to fly near an airport that has an operating control tower. How is radio use by the UA pilot best described?

options.text: Expected to call the tower after launch, but needs no ATC authorization below 400 feet AGL
Not expected to transmit, but should squawk 1200 on a transponder while in that airspace
Not expected to transmit, but should understand the radio traffic and needs ATC authorization in that airspace

questions.explanation: A UA pilot is not expected to talk on aviation frequencies and should refrain from transmitting unless there is an emergency, but listening aids situational awareness. In controlled airspace, prior authorization is required.

questions.prompt: At an airport without an operating control tower, is two-way radio communication required for manned aircraft?

options.text: No, but it is good operating practice to monitor and announce on the CTAF
Yes, because aircraft must announce their position on the CTAF in the traffic pattern
Yes, because aircraft must first get a clearance from the nearest control facility

questions.explanation: Two-way radio is not required at non-towered airports, but pilots should be alert and use the common frequency to announce position and intentions.

questions.prompt: What is a Common Traffic Advisory Frequency (CTAF)?

options.text: A frequency for airport advisory practices at an airport without an operating tower
A frequency for ATC clearances and taxi instructions at an airport with an operating tower
A frequency for continuous automated weather broadcasts at an airport with no control tower

questions.explanation: CTAF may be a UNICOM, MULTICOM, FSS or tower frequency, identified in aeronautical publications. A remote pilot can monitor it for traffic awareness.

questions.prompt: On a sectional chart, how do towered and non-towered airports differ in color?

options.text: Towered airports are blue; others are in black
Towered airports are magenta; others are shown in blue
Towered airports are blue; all others are magenta

questions.explanation: The sectional legend states that airports with control towers are shown in blue and all others in magenta.
questions.source: FAA Chart Users' Guide, VFR Terms and Symbols

questions.prompt: Which sources give a remote pilot airport data such as frequencies, services and closed runways?

options.text: TAFs, METARs, and the manufacturer's operating manuals
Aeronautical charts, the Chart Supplement, and NOTAMs
The PHAK, the Remote Pilot Study Guide, and FAADroneZone

questions.explanation: Three common sources are aeronautical charts, the Chart Supplement U.S. and NOTAMs, plus ATIS for current conditions.

questions.prompt: Before flight, whom must the remote PIC brief about emergency procedures?

options.text: Crew members holding a remote pilot certificate, but not VOs or other uncertificated helpers
The VOs and the person in command, but not a supervised person who is manipulating the controls
Everyone directly participating, including VOs and any non-certificated person at the controls

questions.explanation: Everyone directly participating must be informed about operating conditions, emergency procedures and contingency procedures before the flight.

questions.prompt: What is aeronautical decision-making (ADM)?

options.text: An inborn judgment skill that comes with flight hours and cannot be taught in a classroom
A fixed set of emergency checklists that removes the need for judgment during a flight
A systematic mental process for choosing the best course of action in a given set of circumstances

questions.explanation: ADM gives a structured way to analyze changes during a flight and decide on the best action. Good judgment can be taught.

questions.prompt: What is Crew Resource Management (CRM) in small UA operations?

options.text: A required FAA program: training, testing and certification for VOs and crew
A staffing rule: the crew size, roles and rest needed for each operation
Effective use of all available resources: people, hardware and information

questions.explanation: CRM is a component of ADM in which the remote PIC makes effective use of human resources, hardware and information to maintain a safe operation.

questions.prompt: Which skill belongs to good CRM for a remote PIC leading a team?

options.text: Situational awareness, proper task allocation, avoiding work overload, and effective communication
Letting crew members choose their own tasks, pushing through overload, and speaking up after the flight
Making decisions alone, holding information back from the crew, and taking on extra tasks

questions.explanation: CRM includes situational awareness, allocating tasks, avoiding work overloads and communicating effectively with VOs and others.

questions.prompt: A remote pilot says 'Rules are for others; I know what I'm doing' and ignores the altitude limit. Which hazardous attitude is this?

options.text: Invulnerability
Anti-authority
Resignation

questions.explanation: Anti-authority is 'Don't tell me.' The antidote is 'Follow the rules. They are usually right.'

questions.prompt: What is the first noticeable effect of dehydration?

options.text: Dizziness, which makes precise control inputs difficult
Extreme thirst, which makes it difficult to concentrate
Fatigue, which makes top physical and mental performance difficult

questions.explanation: The first noticeable effect of dehydration is fatigue. Headache, cramps, sleepiness and dizziness follow.

questions.prompt: How does 14 CFR 91.17 limit alcohol use for a remote pilot?

options.text: No flying within 8 hours of drinking unless a test shows an alcohol concentration under 0.04 percent
No flying within 12 hours of drinking or with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more
No flying within 8 hours of drinking or with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 percent or more

questions.explanation: Both limits apply. Even if blood alcohol is below 0.04 percent, a pilot may not fly sooner than 8 hours after drinking.

questions.prompt: What is hyperventilation?

options.text: Breathing too little oxygen at altitude, which causes an abnormal loss of oxygen from the blood
Slow and shallow breathing that causes an abnormal buildup of carbon dioxide in the bloodstream
Excessive rate and depth of breathing, causing abnormal loss of carbon dioxide from the blood

questions.explanation: Hyperventilation seldom incapacitates completely but causes disturbing symptoms. Stress can trigger it.

questions.prompt: About how long do the rods of the eye take to adapt fully to darkness?

options.text: About 30 minutes
About 10 minutes
About 2 hours

questions.explanation: Cones adapt quickly, but the rods take about 30 minutes to fully adapt. A bright light can destroy night adaptation.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred basis for maintaining a small UAS?

options.text: The manufacturer's maintenance instructions and schedule
The part 43 Appendix D checklist and intervals
The remote pilot's own preferred checks and schedule

questions.explanation: Whenever possible, maintain the small UAS and components according to the manufacturer's instructions.
